title: Big Oil and Big Tech Lobby EU for Faster Gas-Fired Data Center Permits | OilPrice.com
text:
Big Oil and Big Tech Lobby EU for Faster Gas-Fired Data Center Permits

Kazakhstan has joined Iraq in asking OPEC+ to raise its estimate of the country's crude production capacity, Reuters reported Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The request comes four days before the group meets to set its output policy for 2027.

The review is OPEC's first, and will assess how much oil each member can produce sustainably, and its findings will help set production targets for next year. One of the sources told Reuters that OPEC+ is holding talks this week with the members that dispute their assessments. US consultancy DeGolyer and MacNaughton is assessing capacity for every OPEC+ member except Russia, Iran and Venezuela. Kazakhstan's energy ministry confirmed the review had taken place but did not comment on its findings or next steps.

Kazakhstan's OPEC+ quota for November and December is 1.628 million barrels per day, according to OPEC data. The International Energy Agency (IEA) estimated Kazakh crude output at 1.76 million bpd in October, about 8% above that target. Chevron began production from the $48 billion Future Growth Project at Kazakhstan's Tengiz field in January 2025.

Export disruptions have also capped Kazakh output this year. The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC), which carries more than 80% of Kazakhstan's oil exports to a terminal near Novorossiysk on Russia's Black Sea coast, suspended loadings in July after drone strikes on tankers at the terminal. Kazakh oil and condensate output fell about 21% to 1.63 million bpd from a July average of 2.07 million bpd, and production at Tengiz fell 56%. In March, the energy ministry had already cut its 2026 production plan to 96–98 million tonnes from 100.5 million tonnes, citing attacks on the CPC and the situation at Tengiz.

Iraq disputes a preliminary finding that puts its capacity at 4.9 million bpd. Baghdad has a quota of 4.431 million bpd and wants OPEC+ to recognize around 6 million bpd of capacity. The IEA puts Iraq's sustainable capacity at 4.87 million bpd. Iraq has warned it may leave OPEC if its quota is not raised, according to Reuters.

The challenges follow the UAE’s exit from OPEC and OPEC+ on May 1. Abu Dhabi had argued for years that its quota did not account for its investment in new capacity. Angola left OPEC in January 2024.

Middle East OPEC+ members have pumped below their quotas for much of 2026 because the Iran war disrupted Gulf flows. Traders are concerned a surplus could build in the rest of 2026 and in 2027 as those flows recover, which has weighed on oil prices.
